actor.description: Recorded actor identity, not host-authenticated authority.

file.description: A staged file relative to the work directory. The consumer verifies its actual bytes against sha256.

relativePath.description: A slash-separated file path relative to the work directory; no absolute path, dot segment, parent traversal, drive prefix or backslash.

context.description: Supporting notes and reference files used to understand the task, separate from its inputs. Empty collections explicitly mean no extra context. Context does not grant additional execution authority.
context.title: Request context

decision.description: .works/<workId>/decisions/<id>.json: an attributed decision on an exact work revision and subject digest. Identity and authority are not authenticated by this schema.
decision.title: Decision

evidence.description: .works/<workId>/evidence/<id>.json: artifact metadata. Existence, actual digest and evidentiary relevance require separate checks.
evidence.title: Evidence

index.description: Version 1 of the proposed .works document format. A document must match exactly one kind. This contract does not migrate or reinterpret legacy session records.
index.title: Works document contract

inputs.description: The prompts and files the request asks the skill to act on. At least one prompt or file is required.
inputs.title: Request inputs

output.description: One produced output. Text is inline; commits identify a repository and full object ID; images and other files bind persisted artifacts. Output metadata alone does not prove correctness or publication.
output.title: Response output

request.description: .works/<workId>/requests/<id>.json: prompts and files to act on, with supporting context kept separate, against one work revision. This record alone grants no execution permission.
request.title: Request

response.description: .works/<workId>/responses/<id>.json: typed outputs produced for one request. Optional verification observations describe their checks separately; delivering an output is not a claim that the work is proved complete.

feedbackRound.description: Completed feedback-and-repair rounds for this request. Initial candidate is round zero; the caller maintains truthful history.

response.title: Response

work.description: .works/<id>/work.json: goal, declared scope, acceptance criteria and current lifecycle.
work.title: Work

@cli/curl.bind: Resolved executable path and reported version in the active environment; working directory and arguments declared by the invocation.
@cli/curl.note: On Windows resolve the curl executable (curl.exe), not a PowerShell alias with different argument semantics. A native web-fetch capability is not this CLI alias.
@cli/curl.purpose: Probe an HTTP endpoint using the curl executable.

@cli/docker.bind: Resolved executable path and reported version in the active environment; working directory and arguments declared by the invocation.
@cli/docker.purpose: Inspect or operate containers and images through Docker CLI.

@cli/git.bind: Resolved executable path and reported version in the active environment; working directory and arguments declared by the invocation.
@cli/git.purpose: Inspect or change Git repository state.

@cli/python.bind: Resolved executable path and reported version in the active environment; working directory and arguments declared by the invocation.
@cli/python.note: Resolve Python 3 from the active environment: python, python3, or py -3 as appropriate; record the selected executable and any launcher arguments.

@cli/shell.bind: Resolved executable path and reported version in the active environment; working directory and arguments declared by the invocation.
@cli/shell.note: Resolve to the session shell (PowerShell, bash or another declared shell); do not assume bash on Windows. Arguments remain separate data until encoded for that shell.
@cli/shell.purpose: Run a declared command in the active session shell.

@tools/fileread.bind: Capability advertised by the active session; availability and invocation permissions checked at use time.
@tools/fileread.purpose: Read declared workspace files and directories through the active session.

claude.via: Claude Code Read, Glob and Grep

@tools/print.bind: Capability advertised by the active session; availability and invocation permissions checked at use time.
@tools/print.purpose: Present text and artifacts in the conversation using the host rendering capabilities.

claude.via: the session's file and render hand-off, which displays an image or an HTML page in the conversation and falls back to the path or the URL

openai.via: the absolute path or the URL printed into the conversation, with the image inline where the client renders one

@tools/sourcewrite.bind: Capability advertised by the active session; availability and invocation permissions checked at use time.
@tools/sourcewrite.purpose: Edit files within the declared write scope through the active session.

@workspaces.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.

@workspaces/artifacts.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.
@workspaces/artifacts.purpose: Produced files, including images, documents and other deliverables.

@workspaces/context.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.
@workspaces/context.purpose: Supporting reference files for a request.

@workspaces/inputs.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.
@workspaces/inputs.purpose: Files supplied as the subject of a request.

@workspaces/requests.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.
@workspaces/requests.purpose: Requests with separate inputs and context.

@workspaces/responses.bind: Explicit absolute root binding from the active invocation; resolve within that root, verify existence when reading, and verify declared write scope before writing.
@workspaces/responses.purpose: Responses declaring produced outputs and execution status.

criteria.history: Record round zero desired state and inventory fingerprint, lease order, fixed-port holders, exact delta, integration provenance and post-effect checks. Every retry begins with fresh inventory and preserves prior effect transcripts.

items.expect: Desired-state, authority, route and inventory evidence match digests.

onFail.instruction: Request exact missing or drifted runtime evidence.

items.expect: The response schema and runtime outputs pass.

onFail.instruction: Repair response metadata from observed runtime artifacts.

items.expect: The response binds this request and revision.
Runtime evidence is present, scoped and digest-bound.

onFail.instruction: Re-read actual delta, checks and receipt files; correct metadata only.

items.expect: Observations reference request criteria and current evidence.
One rung, route, desired-state digest, effect ceiling, capability and authority bind pre-effect inventory.

onFail.instruction: Name the missing authority, capability or mismatched inventory binding.

items.expect: The route keeps its fixed port and no foreign or uncertain holder is reclaimed.

onFail.instruction: Report the port and holder; only its owner may release it.

items.expect: Serve preserves merge provenance, owned conflict scope and passed merged-head gates.

onFail.instruction: Report exact conflict or gate failure; repair must arrive as a new session head.

items.expect: Inventory, allowed effects, mutations and checks match exactly one selected rung.

onFail.instruction: Re-observe and derive a narrower exact delta; do not expand mutable scope.

items.expect: All rung checks and declared endpoint probes prove the recorded generation and served head.

onFail.instruction: Record exact failed probe or check and reassess after targeted authorized repair.

items.expect: Restart, reset, merge and stop effects are never repeated while completion is uncertain.

onFail.instruction: Stop and require authoritative entry, process and head observation before any effect.

items.expect: Registry, Git, process, container and probe capabilities needed by the rung are available.

onFail.instruction: Return the missing capability; do not substitute a wider mechanism.

items.expect: Route, rung, desired state, authority, fixed ports and inventory are complete.

onFail.instruction: Ask for the exact missing binding before effects.

items.expect: Every runtime effect has known completion.

onFail.instruction: Observe and re-inventory the entry, process, port and served head first; never blindly repeat the effect.

criteria.stopWhen: Stop after two feedback rounds, repeated rung failure, port conflict, missing authority, failed merged-head gate, unavailable capability or unobservable uncertain effect. Never rebase, force or reclaim a foreign port.

purpose: Climb one requested rung of the runtime ladder for one bound product route, preserve its fixed port and integration branch, and attest the resulting entry from live probes.

request.description: Bind one route key, one runtime-ladder rung, fixed port claims, the desired-state digest and allowed effects, current inventory, registry capability custody and existing environment authority. A serve request also binds the session commit and changed-file ownership.
request.title: runtime.serve request

response.description: A done response retains the inventory and applied delta, complete rung check set, route entry, fixed port, generation and attested served head. A proved already-converged result includes paired observations and no mutation.
response.title: runtime.serve response

scope: One route and one rung: stack-up, locate, start-role, serve, restart, reset or stop. Effects require existing authority; foreign holders are never reclaimed; integration uses merge commits and gates the merged head without rebase or force.

calls.purpose: Read desired state, authority and inventory evidence.
Read routed checkout and commit provenance.

steps.instruction: Read the request and declared current inventory. Bind one route key, one ladder rung, fixed port claims, desired-state digest, allowed effects, mutable ceiling, capability custody, environment authority, and session commit plus owned paths for serve. No declaration grants itself authority.

Re-observe the route entry, process, generation, served head, configuration, health and every fixed-port holder before effects. Classify reusable, missing, invalid, foreign or uncertain state and acquire the declared lease order.

calls.purpose: Merge and verify the integration head without rebase or force.

calls.when: for stack-up, start-role, restart, reset or stop when container-backed

calls.purpose: Run declared role, gate and process commands.
calls.when: when required by the selected rung

calls.purpose: Persist the exact allowed and applied delta.

steps.instruction: Perform only the selected rung's allowed delta under the lease. Reuse already-converged state. For serve, merge the session commit into the fixed integration branch without rebase or force, resolve only owned rule-covered hunks, gate the merged head, then operate the one detached server. Never reclaim a foreign port.

reads.when: when the rung needs a checkout

writes.when: only for the serve rung's integration merge

calls.when: unless the selected rung is stop

steps.instruction: After any mutation or uncertain result, re-inventory the entry, process, port and served head before further commands. Probe every declared endpoint and collect the rung's complete check set. A converged no-op uses paired read-only observations and records zero mutations.

Compare authority, inventory, fixed ports, integration provenance, delta and attestation. Produce exact defects and a receipt only when every required rung check passes; uncertain effects remain observed and never blindly repeated.
produces: Concrete failed-criterion feedback or passing review results.

calls.purpose: Present the attested route, generation and served head.

steps.instruction: Write and validate the response with exact hashes, observations and review results. Present the route as serving only from passed endpoint and rung evidence; stop results show the released holder instead.

validate.failurePolicy: Turn failed checks into exact inventory, port, integration or probe defects. Repair within two rounds, re-observe before effect retries, and block wider or unauthorized changes.

review.instruction: Confirm route, rung, desired-state digest, mutable ceiling, allowed effects, capability custody, inventory fingerprint and environment authority were bound before any effect.
Confirm the route keeps its declared fixed port, every holder is identified, and no foreign or uncertain process is stopped or reconfigured to reclaim a port.

For serve, verify the session commit is contained in the served head, integration uses merge or valid fast-forward without rebase or force, conflicts touch only owned hunks under closed rules, and gates pass on the merged head.
Match inventory, requested effects, applied mutations and check set to the selected runtime rung. Already-converged results have paired read-only proof and zero mutations.
Probe every declared endpoint and bind the answering process, generation, integration branch and served head. A missing or failed rung check cannot be described as serving.
On uncertain completion, inventory the entry, process and served head again before any command. Reuse converged state and never blindly repeat restart, reset, merge or stop.
